title: Massive Upper GI Bleed
brief: A 58-year-old man with alcohol use disorder arrives vomiting blood from esophageal varices and says he only needs a beer. Learners practice early blood transfusion, variceal bleed drugs and airway protection in massive GI bleeding.

title: TB Pericarditis
brief: A 38-year-old Ethiopian refugee with untreated HIV and past tuberculosis comes in with chest pain and severe shortness of breath from a large pericardial effusion. Learners must recognize tamponade, drain the effusion and think of TB in a patient with HIV.

title: Newborn Resuscitation
brief: A baby is born suddenly in the emergency department to a mother with no prenatal care who uses IV drugs, and the newborn is flat. Learners run the neonatal resuscitation algorithm as a team.

title: Newborn Sepsis with Apneas
brief: A 3-day-old term baby has poor feeding, vomiting and a temperature of 33.1 C, then has apnea spells. Learners recognize neonatal sepsis, treat low glucose and low temperature, support breathing and give early antibiotics.

title: Breech Delivery + NRP
brief: A 19-year-old woman who denies pregnancy arrives in active labor and the baby is breech. Learners prepare the room, assist a breech birth and resuscitate the newborn.

title: Postpartum Hemorrhage and NRP
brief: A 26-year-old woman at 38 weeks delivers in the emergency department; the baby needs full resuscitation and the mother then bleeds heavily. Learners manage neonatal resuscitation and postpartum hemorrhage at the same time.

title: Eclampsia with Apnea Secondary to Magnesium Sulfate Administration
brief: A 30-year-old first-time mother at 32 weeks has headache, blurred vision, vomiting and a blood pressure of 175/115, then seizes. Learners give magnesium early, add a blood pressure drug and treat magnesium-induced apnea with calcium.

title: Late Post Partum Pre-eclampsia
authors: Meassick K, Butler S, Italiya S
brief: A 20-year-old woman five weeks after delivery has upper belly pain, vomiting, breathlessness and high blood pressure. Learners recognize late postpartum preeclampsia and start treatment.

title: Acute Chest Syndrome
brief: A 4-year-old boy with sickle cell disease (HbSS) has cough, fever and low oxygen. Learners recognize acute chest syndrome and start oxygen, antibiotics, pain control and transfusion planning.

title: Pediatric DKA
brief: An 8-year-old girl with new diabetic ketoacidosis is referred from another hospital after a fluid bolus and an insulin bolus. Learners set safe fluid and insulin plans and watch for cerebral edema.

title: DKA
brief: An 8-year-old girl with three days of tiredness, vomiting and belly pain becomes confused. Learners diagnose severe diabetic ketoacidosis and manage its complex physiology, including repeat glucose checks.

title: Dysrhythmia Secondary to Hyperkalemia
brief: A 52-year-old man with diabetes, hypertension and kidney failure on dialysis missed a session and now feels weak and dizzy, with an ECG that looks like a heart attack. Learners recognize severe high potassium and treat it fast.

title: Nightmares Case 5: Pulmonary Edema
brief: A man admitted with a hip fracture is given maintenance fluids while his usual medicines are held and wakes up short of breath with low oxygen. New residents assess and treat acute pulmonary edema.

title: Aortic Stenosis with A Fib and CHF
brief: A 78-year-old man with severe aortic stenosis has four days of worse breathlessness, new atrial fibrillation at 150 and low oxygen. Learners adjust heart failure and rate control treatment for a fixed valve narrowing.

title: Nightmares Case 12: Hypertensive Encephalopathy
brief: A 73-year-old man on the surgical ward before bowel surgery becomes confused with chest heaviness and breathlessness at 3 am. New residents recognize hypertensive encephalopathy and lower blood pressure safely.

title: COPDE with Pneumothorax
brief: A 68-year-old man with COPD on home oxygen arrives hypoxic, hypercarbic and agitated and needs intubation, then develops a pneumothorax. Learners manage respiratory failure and spot complications of their own treatment.

title: Pediatric Septic Shock
brief: A 4-year-old girl with three days of fever and cough is lethargic and not herself. Learners recognize early septic shock, get IV or intraosseous access fast and give fluids and antibiotics.

title: Urologic Sepsis
authors: Huang J, Dowhos K, Colpitts L
brief: A 59-year-old woman with a past heart attack and a weak heart has a week of urinary symptoms, fever and flank pain. Learners treat septic shock while balancing fluids in a patient with heart failure.

title: Intra-abdominal Sepsis
brief: A 60-year-old man with four days of belly pain from cholangitis arrives in septic shock at a community hospital. Learners find the source, start broad antibiotics and give fluids and vasopressors.

title: Nightmares Case 2: Pneumonia
brief: A 64-year-old man in hospital for three days with community-acquired pneumonia is getting more short of breath despite antibiotics. New residents reassess a deteriorating ward patient and escalate care.

title: Bronchiolitis
brief: A 6-month-old girl with a cold from an older sibling now has noisy breathing and is not feeding. Learners assess and support an infant with bronchiolitis and review which treatments help.

title: Alcohol and opioid use
brief: A 29-year-old man falls in the shower while drunk and cannot remember the event. After the trauma work-up, learners use screening, brief intervention and referral to treatment (SBIRT) with a live patient conversation.

title: Acetaminophen Overdose with an Uncooperative Patient
brief: A 25-year-old man took a large acetaminophen overdose to end his life and is irritable and refuses treatment. Learners treat the poisoning while addressing suicide risk, capacity and mental health law.

title: Tricyclic Antidepressant Overdose
brief: A 27-year-old man has an intentional amitriptyline overdose with a wide QRS and later cardiac arrest. Learners give sodium bicarbonate and manage a toxic arrest.

title: MVC with Tension Pneumothorax
brief: A 44-year-old driver in a highway-speed crash arrives screaming with a GCS of 13. Learners run a primary and secondary survey and decompress a tension pneumothorax without waiting for imaging.

title: Pediatric Polytrauma
brief: A 2.5-year-old falls 9 m from a balcony and arrives at a community hospital in compensated shock, with upset family present. Learners coordinate a pediatric trauma survey and resuscitation under stress.

title: Pediatric Traumatic Brain Injury
authors: De Santis D, Klowak JA, Ngo Q
brief: An 18-month-old falls from a play structure, loses consciousness and is irritable with an obvious head injury. Learners manage severe pediatric head injury and raised brain pressure.

title: Organophosphate Poisoning
brief: A 60-year-old berry farmer who hand-sprayed pesticide has vomiting, diarrhea, copious secretions, slow heart rate and low oxygen. Learners recognize the cholinergic toxidrome and give atropine and pralidoxime.

title: Subarachnoid Hemorrhage with Increased Intracranial Pressure
brief: A 45-year-old man collapses at the gym after a sudden severe headache and arrives unconscious. Learners control blood pressure, intubate safely and treat raised brain pressure from a brain bleed.

title: Ruptured Ectopic
brief: A 26-year-old recent immigrant from Cambodia with limited English faints at home after days of vomiting. Learners check a pregnancy test in any young woman with syncope and resuscitate internal bleeding from ectopic pregnancy.

title: Pregnant Cardiomyopathy
brief: A 38-year-old woman at 36 weeks with weeks of ignored symptoms faints at home and is in acute heart failure. Learners manage pregnancy-related cardiomyopathy and plan care for mother and baby.

title: International Pediatric Emergency Medicine and Critical Care Fellow Education: Utilizing Virtual Resuscitation Simulation in Settings With Differing Resources (Case 1: Joseph, diarrhea and hypovolemic shock)
brief: Joseph, 3 years old, comes to a rural clinic in Kenya after seven days of watery diarrhea and is in shock. Learners use the WHO shock definition, check dehydration and malnutrition, give fluids and glucose and decide on referral.

title: International Pediatric Emergency Medicine and Critical Care Fellow Education: Utilizing Virtual Resuscitation Simulation in Settings With Differing Resources (Case 2: Stephen, diarrhea with electrolyte derangement)
brief: Stephen, 2 years old, arrives at a district hospital with eight days of profuse watery diarrhea and shock; labs show high sodium and low potassium. If the salts are not corrected he goes into pulseless VT, so learners practice fluids, electrolyte correction, CPR and defibrillation.

title: International Pediatric Emergency Medicine and Critical Care Fellow Education: Utilizing Virtual Resuscitation Simulation in Settings With Differing Resources (Case 3: Jane, fever and septic shock)
brief: Jane, 12 months old, has five days of fever and one day of lethargy and meets the WHO definition of shock at a central hospital. Learners give fluids, oxygen and antibiotics and then manage fluid overload that leads to intubation.

title: A Simulation Scenario Focused on Resuscitation of a Young Infant (Neonate) for Nurses and Midwives in Malawi, a Limited Resource Country
brief: Nana, a 7-week-old girl sent from the under-five clinic, looks unwell and has noisy breathing. Nursing and midwifery students in Malawi practice ABC assessment, bag-mask ventilation, CPR and post-resuscitation care with local low-cost equipment.

title: Postpartum Magnesium Sulfate Overdose: A Multidisciplinary and Interprofessional Simulation Scenario
brief: A postpartum woman with preeclampsia on magnesium sulfate for seizure prevention develops magnesium toxicity and stops breathing. Obstetric, anesthesia and nursing teams practice recognizing toxicity, giving calcium and supporting breathing.

title: Effectiveness of Simulation-Based Training of Undergraduate Medical Students Regarding the Management of Eclampsia: A Randomized Controlled Educational Trial
brief: A trial at AIIMS Hyderabad, India, built and tested a simulation module on managing an eclamptic seizure. It gives a tested eclampsia training design for undergraduate medical students in an Indian teaching hospital.

title: Impact of an Obstetrical Emergency Simulation Learning Module on Midwifery Students' Competency: A Non-randomized Control Study
brief: A study from Chennai, India, used five staged simulation scenarios (eclampsia, antepartum hemorrhage, cord prolapse, prolonged labor and postpartum hemorrhage) with 16 OSCE stations for midwifery students. It aligns with Indian Nursing Council and WHO skilled birth attendant guidance.

title: Pediatric Rattlesnake Envenomation: A Simulation Scenario With Optional Health Equity, Virtual Facilitation, and Senior Learner Modifications
brief: Carlos, a 3-year-old boy at a campsite, comes in crying and holding his arm after an unwitnessed snakebite. Learners recognize envenomation, give antivenom and treat an antivenom reaction, with optional health equity and virtual versions.

title: Pediatric Motor Vehicle-Pedestrian Accident: a Simulation Scenario for Emergency Medicine Trainees
brief: An 8-year-old boy struck by a pick-up truck arrives at a rural emergency department with femur and elbow fractures, 90 minutes from a trauma center. Learners run pediatric trauma care and arrange transfer.

title: Prehospital Trauma Care: A Simulation Scenario for Rural-Based Healthcare Providers
brief: A two-vehicle crash on a rural highway 80 km from hospital leaves several casualties, some ejected. Rural providers practice scene safety, triage and stabilization before transport.

title: Initial Resuscitation of a Multisystem Trauma Patient Following a Fall From Height: A Complete Simulation Scenario for Medical Students
brief: A 25-year-old man falls 20 feet and has an open femur fracture, bleeding, tension pneumothorax and head injury. Medical students practice the primary survey and early trauma resuscitation.

title: Diabetic Ketoacidosis: An Emergency Medicine Simulation Scenario
brief: A 19-year-old man in his first weekend at a university dormitory is found with vomiting, weakness and low consciousness, with few details known. Learners diagnose new diabetic ketoacidosis and manage fluids, insulin and potassium.

title: Two Simulation Cases to Prepare for a Public Festival: Pediatric Methylenedioxymethamphetamine (MDMA) Ingestion and Alcohol Toxicity
brief: A 15-year-old is found lying on the ground at a hot summer music festival, drunk with slurred speech, with an older sibling present (a second case covers MDMA toxicity). Staff practice medical care of intoxication and the social and safeguarding side of the case.

title: Chest Pain on the Ward: A Simulation Scenario for Rural Family and Emergency Medicine Trainees
brief: A patient admitted earlier in the day at a rural hospital develops chest pain on the ward and goes into cardiogenic shock from acute coronary syndrome. Rural family and emergency trainees practice recognition and stabilization.

title: Diagnosis and Management of an Inferior ST-elevation Myocardial Infarction: A Simulation Scenario
brief: A 51-year-old has two hours of epigastric pain that antacids do not help. Learners recognize an inferior STEMI, treat it and follow ACLS if it deteriorates.

title: Necrotizing Fasciitis: An Emergency Medicine Simulation Scenario
brief: A 68-year-old woman who fell during yard work the day before has hip pain and is becoming septic. Learners diagnose necrotizing fasciitis, start treatment and advocate for surgery when consultants push back.

title: Simulation of an Atypical Presentation of Necrotizing Enterocolitis in the Emergency Department
brief: A term newborn comes to the emergency center with bowel inflammation (necrotizing enterocolitis) caused by a urinary infection and bloodstream infection. Learners recognize a septic infant and resuscitate with PALS.

title: Asthma Exacerbation: An Emergency Medicine Simulation Scenario
brief: A 23-year-old woman with asthma and past ICU admissions comes in short of breath after a recent course of prednisone. Learners manage a severe asthma attack, with difficulty adjusted to the learner level.

title: EM ReSCu Peds: Case 5 | Diabetic Ketoacidosis
license: Free access; ALiEM content All Rights Reserved
brief: An 8-year-old girl lies miserable with vomiting and belly pain and dry lips, with an anxious mother at the bedside. Learners diagnose pediatric DKA and manage fluids and insulin safely.

title: EM ReSCu Peds: Case 13 | Pneumonia and Septic Shock
license: Free access; ALiEM content All Rights Reserved
brief: A 10-year-old boy with a tracheostomy has had a week of cough and fever and now cannot keep his oxygen above 85%. Learners manage pneumonia with septic shock and airway problems in a medically complex child.

title: EM ReSCu Peds: Case 9 | Neonatal Delivery
authors: Tay KY, Sanseau E, Carr L
license: Free access; ALiEM content All Rights Reserved
brief: A mother arrives in the emergency department and the newborn of unknown gestational age is limp, blue and not breathing. Learners run neonatal resuscitation from the first minute.

title: EM ReSCu Peds: Case 7 | Multisystem Trauma
license: Free access; ALiEM content All Rights Reserved
brief: A 6-year-old girl ran into the street after a ball and was hit by a car; she has slow shallow breathing and a deformed leg. Learners run a pediatric trauma resuscitation.

title: EM ReSCu Peds: Case 14 | Status Asthmaticus
license: Free access; ALiEM content All Rights Reserved
brief: A 6-year-old boy is quiet, in severe respiratory distress with poor air entry. Learners escalate treatment for life-threatening asthma.

title: SimBox: A Postpartum Complication
authors: Athanasopoulou S, Cohen S, Auerbach M, Kou M, Sanseau E
brief: A 16-year-old who did not know she was pregnant arrives by ambulance in active labor with vaginal bleeding. The emergency team manages postpartum hemorrhage and decides where to transfer.

title: SimBox: Newborn Resuscitation
brief: A 16-year-old in active labor who learned of her pregnancy that day delivers in the emergency department. The team resuscitates the newborn, with a low-cost doll or mannequin and a video monitor.

title: SimBox: A Sick Neonate (Neonatal Shock)
brief: A 7-day-old term baby boy is brought in by ambulance lethargic and very unwell. The team treats neonatal shock with fluids, glucose, warmth and antibiotics and works through causes including sepsis and heart disease.

title: SimBox: Infant with Respiratory Distress (Bronchiolitis)
brief: A 4-month-old boy has four days of cough, congestion and poor feeding, breathing at 80 per minute with oxygen at 86%. The team supports breathing in bronchiolitis and plans transfer.

title: SimBox: Diabetic Ketoacidosis (DKA)
brief: A previously healthy 10-year-old girl with weeks of thirst and frequent urination is sleepy and pale with slow capillary refill. The team diagnoses DKA and starts evidence-based treatment.

title: SimBox: Suicide Risk Assessment
authors: Mielke B, Hilliard M, Simpson L, Brenner A
brief: A 12-year-old girl seen for abdominal pain screens at moderate suicide risk. Clinicians practice a full suicide risk assessment (SAFE-T or BSSA), set the risk level and build a safety plan.

title: SimBox: Suicide Screen - Nursing
authors: Mielke B, Brenner A, Hilliard M, Simpson L
brief: A 12-year-old girl arrives at triage with abdominal pain and poor appetite. Nurses practice asking the suicide screening questions (ASQ or C-SSRS), handling barriers and acting on a positive screen.

title: SimBox: Severe Head Injury
brief: A 5-year-old boy who was not properly restrained in a high-speed car crash has a scalp hematoma and then a large epidural bleed. The team scores his mental state, intubates and treats raised brain pressure.

title: COPD exacerbation assessment and intervention
brief: A client has an acute COPD exacerbation. Nursing students do priority assessments and start care based on RNAO COPD guidelines.

title: Acute Depression
brief: A patient with acute depression and suicidal thoughts has been admitted voluntarily to a psychiatric unit. Nursing students practice a trauma-informed interview, mental status exam and suicide risk assessment in a virtual patient.

title: Assessing Suicide Risk & Responding
brief: A virtual patient has suicidal thoughts. Nursing students use the SAFE-T protocol with the C-SSRS to judge risk, share safety concerns with the team and make a safe care plan.

title: Pediatric Sepsis ("Harper Peterson")
brief: A critically ill infant needs paramedic stabilization before transport. Paramedic students recognize septic shock, treat circulatory failure and decide when to intubate.

title: Congenital cerebral malaria: a masquerader in a neonate
brief: A 5-day-old baby in Nigeria looks like he has neonatal sepsis, jaundice and then meningitis, but a blood film shows malaria parasites. Learners practice a neonatal fever workup and remember to test for malaria in newborns in endemic areas.

title: Poor response to artesunate treatment in two patients with severe malaria on the Thai-Myanmar border
learner: Residents, internal medicine and ID trainees
brief: Two adults with severe falciparum malaria on the Thai-Myanmar border respond poorly to IV artesunate; one dies and one clears parasites only after 11 days. Learners recognize severe malaria, monitor parasite clearance and think about artemisinin resistance.
learners: Residents, internal medicine and ID trainees

title: Duodenal perforation in a 12-month old child with severe malaria
brief: A 1-year-old in Ghana with confirmed severe malaria also has a perforated duodenal ulcer, and the malaria result delays the surgical diagnosis. Learners practice keeping a wide differential when a febrile child has a positive malaria test.

title: Severe retinal whitening in an adult with cerebral malaria
license: ASTMH re-use licence (non-commercial use with citation)
brief: A retinal photo of a 24-year-old Bangladeshi man with non-fatal cerebral malaria shows severe malarial retinopathy. Use it as an exam finding card when an SP portrays a comatose patient with cerebral malaria.

title: Plasmodium vivax cerebral malaria in an adult patient in Sudan
brief: A 60-year-old man in Khartoum develops cerebral malaria caused by P. vivax, not P. falciparum. Learners learn that vivax can be severe and that species testing matters in Africa.

title: Gorgas Case 2025-9 (uncomplicated Plasmodium vivax malaria)
authors: Gorgas Course, UAB and Universidad Peruana Cayetano Heredia
license: Free access; no open licence stated
brief: An 18-year-old woman comes to a Lima emergency department with 5 days of fever, chills, headache and dark urine. Learners take a travel and exposure history and confirm malaria with a rapid test and blood smear.

title: An 11-month-old boy with tuberculous meningitis presenting as progressive limb weakness, fever, developmental retardation, and loss of consciousness: a case report
brief: An 11-month-old boy in Iran loses milestones and develops limb weakness, fever and reduced consciousness over weeks, and is treated successfully for TB meningitis. Learners take a developmental and TB contact history from a parent and recognize subacute meningitis.

title: Use of alternative cerebrospinal fluid-based biomarkers to help diagnose Xpert-negative tuberculous meningitis: A case report
brief: A 5-year-old boy in Nepal has 2 weeks of evening fever, headache and vomiting, then a seizure and left-sided weakness while on antibiotics for presumed bacterial meningitis. Learners see that a negative Xpert test does not rule out TB meningitis and use CSF markers to decide.

title: Drug-resistant tuberculosis treatment complicated by antiretroviral resistance in HIV coinfected patients: a report of six cases in Lesotho
learner: Residents, HIV and TB program clinicians
brief: Six patients in Lesotho on drug-resistant TB treatment also have HIV that no longer responds to their antiretroviral drugs. Learners plan care for MDR-TB with HIV where viral load and resistance tests are scarce.
learners: Residents, HIV and TB program clinicians

title: Lung abscess complicating a case of multidrug-resistant tuberculosis
brief: A 54-year-old man in India who stopped TB treatment after 2 months returns with blood-tinged sputum and a cavity with a lung abscess, later found to be MDR-TB. Learners explore reasons for stopping treatment and counsel on adherence.

title: Gorgas Case 2026-11 (Pott's disease)
authors: Gorgas Course, UAB and Universidad Peruana Cayetano Heredia
license: Free access; no open licence stated
brief: A 39-year-old man from Barranca, Peru, has 10 months of back pain, a growing back mass, weight loss, night sweats, cough and then leg weakness. Learners link back pain and red flags to spinal TB and ask about TB treatment history.

title: Self-Study Module 4: Treatment of Latent Tuberculosis Infection and Tuberculosis Disease (case studies 4.1 to 4.7)
learner: Nurses, medical students, community health workers
brief: Short case studies include a household contact visit, a drinker on isoniazid, a toddler with TB meningitis and a patient worried that her urine has changed color. Each is a ready prompt for a brief treatment counseling role-play with an answer key.
learners: Nurses, medical students, community health workers

title: Self-Study Module 6: Managing Tuberculosis Patients and Improving Adherence (case studies 6.1 to 6.6)
learner: Nurses, case managers, community health workers
brief: Case studies include a restaurant cook newly diagnosed with smear-positive TB and a recent immigrant from India who starts missing directly observed therapy. Learners assess beliefs about TB and solve adherence barriers.
learners: Nurses, case managers, community health workers

title: Tuberculosis Radiology Practice Cases
authors: Curry International Tuberculosis Center and Firland Northwest TB Center
license: Free access; copyright Regents of the University of California
brief: Brief interactive cases where learners find abnormal areas on chest X-rays in real clinical scenarios. Use the images as investigation results inside a TB SP station.

title: Evaluation of a Headache in Advanced HIV (Case Discussions, Season 1 Episode 2)
license: Free access; copyright University of Washington
brief: A 28-year-old man newly diagnosed with HIV and a CD4 count of 4 has 2 weeks of headache, photophobia, blurred vision and vomiting. Learners recognize possible cryptococcal meningitis and plan urgent imaging and lumbar puncture; a follow-up episode covers treatment.

title: Evaluation of Focal Neurological Symptoms in a Patient with Advanced HIV (Case Discussions, Season 1 Episode 7)
license: Free access; copyright University of Washington
brief: A 27-year-old man with HIV has a headache that started 2 to 3 weeks ago and new focal neurological symptoms. Learners build a differential for brain lesions in advanced HIV, including toxoplasmosis.

title: Ischemic stroke as a complication of cryptococcal meningitis and immune reconstitution inflammatory syndrome: a case report
brief: A 38-year-old man in Blantyre, Malawi, newly diagnosed with HIV, has 2 weeks of headache and vomiting and is treated for cryptococcal meningitis, then has a stroke after starting ART. Learners manage raised CSF pressure and recognize IRIS.

title: Cryptococcal meningitis and immune reconstitution inflammatory syndrome in a pediatric patient with HIV after switching to second line antiretroviral therapy: a case report
brief: A 10-year-old girl with HIV in Uganda develops severe headache and seizures 8 weeks after switching to second-line ART, and has cryptococcal meningitis. Learners take a pediatric HIV treatment history with a caregiver and recognize IRIS.

title: Acute vision loss in post-partum period as presenting symptom of HIV-associated cryptococcal meningitis: an unusual case report
brief: A 25-year-old woman in India loses vision in both eyes after giving birth and is found to have HIV and cryptococcal meningitis. Learners widen the differential for postpartum neurological symptoms and handle a new HIV diagnosis sensitively.

title: Pulmonary cryptococcosis presenting as acute severe respiratory distress in a newly diagnosed HIV patient in Tanzania: a case report
brief: A patient newly diagnosed with HIV in Mwanza, Tanzania, has severe breathing difficulty and dies after pulmonary cryptococcosis is missed. Learners think beyond TB and PCP when a patient with advanced HIV is short of breath.

title: Gorgas Case 2023-04 (presumptive dengue without alarm signs)
authors: Gorgas Course, UAB and Universidad Peruana Cayetano Heredia
license: Free access; no open licence stated
brief: A 20-year-old medical student has 7 days of high fever, headache, eye pain, joint pain and a spreading rash after a trip home to the Peruvian jungle. Learners take a travel history, check for warning signs and rule out malaria.

title: Dengue shock syndrome complicated with acute liver failure and kidney injury, infective endocarditis, and deep vein thrombosis: a case report
brief: A 38-year-old woman in Colombo, Sri Lanka, develops dengue shock with liver and kidney failure and later bacterial complications. Learners practice fluid management and close monitoring in the critical phase of dengue.

title: Expanded dengue syndrome presenting with acute liver failure, acute kidney injury, pancreatic involvement, coagulopathy, and multiple intracranial hemorrhages in a young child: a case report
brief: A 6-year-old girl in Sri Lanka has 5 days of fever, bloody diarrhea, blood in the urine and a swollen knee, and develops multi-organ dengue. Learners recognize warning signs in a child and escalate care early.

title: Case Report: Dengue Fever Progressing to Acute Liver Failure and Hepatic Encephalopathy
brief: A young man in Indore, India, with dengue develops liver failure and confusion without shock. Learners see that dengue can present with severe organ involvement and learn which tests to follow.

title: Case Report: Typhoid Fever Complicated by Ileal Perforation in an Urban Slum of Dhaka, Bangladesh
learner: Medical students, surgical and medicine trainees
brief: A 19-year-old man in a Dhaka urban slum has high fever, lower abdominal pain and vomiting, and has a typhoid ileal perforation. Learners recognize an acute abdomen in typhoid and plan urgent surgery and antibiotics.
learners: Medical students, surgical and medicine trainees

title: Severe thrombocytopenia in a child with typhoid fever: a case report
brief: A 4-year-old boy returning from travel has a long fever and a very low platelet count, and blood culture shows typhoid. Learners take a travel and food history from a parent and manage low platelets without transfusion.

title: A case of typhoid fever with neurological presentation
brief: A 31-year-old man in Dhaka has 18 days of fever, headache, rash, diarrhea, confusion and blurred vision, with sixth nerve palsies. Learners include typhoid in the differential of prolonged fever with neurological signs.

title: Fatal case of meningococcal meningitis in a child from rural Bhutan: A case report
brief: A 10-year-old boy in rural Bhutan comes home from school with fever and body aches, becomes drowsy overnight and has a purpuric rash. Learners recognize meningococcal disease fast, give antibiotics before transfer and notify public health.

title: Presumed Meningococcal meningitis with Waterhouse-Friderichsen syndrome from a rural Ethiopia: a fatal case report and literature review
license: CC BY-NC-ND 4.0 (Annals of Medicine and Surgery)
brief: An unvaccinated 35-year-old woman in rural Ethiopia has 24 hours of fever, headache and neck pain, then confusion, low blood pressure and a spreading purpuric rash. Learners manage septic shock with meningitis in a low-resource hospital.

title: Disseminated melioidosis: challenge to routine antibiotic therapy: a case report
brief: A middle-aged man with diabetes in Raipur, India, has high fever, breathlessness and a swollen knee and ankle, first misdiagnosed as TB. Learners consider melioidosis in septic diabetic patients in South and Southeast Asia.

title: Amoebic Dysentery Complicated by Hypovolemic Shock and Sepsis in an Infant with Severe Acute Malnutrition: A Case Report
brief: A 10-month-old boy with severe acute malnutrition is admitted in Port Sudan with bloody diarrhea, shock and sepsis. Learners apply careful fluid and antibiotic rules for malnourished children with diarrhea.

title: Optimizing survival in Russell's viper bite cases in low-resource setting: two case reports
learner: Medical students, emergency and medicine trainees
brief: Two men in rural Bangladesh go to traditional healers after Russell's viper bites and arrive late with bleeding problems and kidney failure. Learners take a bite history, run a 20-minute clotting test and plan antivenom and dialysis.
learners: Medical students, emergency and medicine trainees

title: Confirmed Ceylon krait (Bungarus ceylonicus) envenoming in Sri Lanka resulting in neuromuscular paralysis: a case report
brief: A 26-year-old man in Sri Lanka bitten by a krait develops droopy eyelids, eye movement weakness, facial weakness and trouble swallowing. Learners check for neurotoxic signs and watch for breathing failure.

title: Priapism following a juvenile Russell's viper bite: An unusual case report
brief: A 16-year-old boy in India develops a painful erection soon after a Russell's viper bite, which settles after antivenom. Learners handle a sensitive history with an adolescent and recognize systemic envenoming.

title: Vibrio vulnificus sepsis following Naja atra Snakebite: A rare case report from Vietnam
brief: An 80-year-old woman collecting fish on the coast of Thai Binh, Vietnam, is bitten by a cobra and arrives 18 hours later with tissue death and septic shock. Learners combine antivenom, antibiotics, dialysis and surgery.

title: Shortcomings in snake bite management in rural Cameroon: a case report
brief: A 10-year-old boy from a remote area of Cameroon arrives 12 hours after a snakebite to the face with severe envenoming, and antivenom is out of stock. Learners manage envenoming with limited antivenom and talk with the family about delays in care.

title: Revered but Poorly Understood: A Case Report of Dendroaspis polylepis (Black Mamba) Envenomation in Watamu, Malindi Kenya, and a Review of the Literature
license: CC BY 4.0 (Tropical Medicine and Infectious Disease)
brief: A 13-year-old boy in coastal Kenya arrives at a small hospital with labored breathing, frothing, severe ptosis, unrecordable blood pressure and low oxygen after a black mamba bite. Learners run a resuscitation with airway support and antivenom.

title: Snake bite in third trimester of pregnancy with systemic envenomation and delivery of a live baby in a low resource setting: A case report
license: CC BY-NC-ND 4.0 (Case Reports in Women's Health)
brief: A 22-year-old woman in Nigeria at 32 weeks, living with HIV, arrives late after a snakebite with leg swelling, vaginal bleeding, labor pains and shock. Learners coordinate obstetric and envenoming care in a low-resource setting.

title: Gorgas Case 2022-04 (mild envenoming by desert lance-headed pit viper)
authors: Gorgas Course, UAB and Universidad Peruana Cayetano Heredia
license: Free access; no open licence stated
brief: A 53-year-old woman is bitten on the finger while washing dishes outside, pours kerosene on her arm, and arrives 2 hours later with swelling to the armpit and bruising. Learners take a bite history, address harmful first aid and decide on antivenom.

title: Orbital compression syndrome in a Ugandan child with sickle cell disease: A case report
brief: An 11-year-old boy with sickle cell disease at Mulago Hospital, Kampala, has a week of swollen eyelids, bulging eyes, reduced vision, fever and headache. Learners take a sickle cell history, including prophylaxis and transfusions, and rule out orbital infection.

title: Hair-on-End Sign in a 9-Year-Old Girl Presenting with Acute Stroke in Sickle Cell Disease
license: CC BY-NC 3.0 (International Medical Case Reports Journal)
brief: A 9-year-old girl in Uganda has a stroke, and tests then confirm she has sickle cell anemia. Learners recognize stroke in a child with sickle cell disease and discuss stroke prevention with the family.

title: Orbital Compression Syndrome Mimicking Severe Malaria in a Child with Sickle Cell Disease in a Ugandan Refugee Settlement: A Case Report
license: CC BY-NC 4.0 (International Medical Case Reports Journal)
brief: A 9-year-old boy with sickle cell disease at a clinic in Palabek refugee settlement, northern Uganda, has sudden headache, high fever and swelling around both eyes. Learners avoid anchoring on malaria and manage the child in a primary care humanitarian setting.

title: Diabetic-ketoacidosis in a nine-year-old child with homozygous sickle cell anaemia: a rare case report
brief: A 9-year-old with sickle cell anemia in Katsina, Nigeria, has abdominal pain that looks like a sickle crisis but is also in diabetic ketoacidosis. Learners check glucose in a sick child with sickle cell disease and correct fluids safely.

title: Preterm management of sickle cell crisis in a twin pregnancy with suboptimal antenatal care in a primary healthcare facility: A case report from Cameroon and literature review
brief: A 21-year-old woman with sickle cell disease and a twin pregnancy has painful crises at a primary care facility in Cameroon with no blood bank. Learners manage a crisis in pregnancy and plan referral with limited resources.

title: Rheumatic heart disease in pregnancy: a report of 2 cases
brief: Two pregnant women in Harare, Zimbabwe, have rheumatic heart disease; one with severe mitral stenosis dies after delivery from an arrhythmia. Learners plan antenatal care, anticoagulation choices and delivery for women with RHD.

title: Reversible Ortner's syndrome in a woman with decompensated rheumatic heart disease: a case report
brief: A 48-year-old farmer in Nepal who had a mitral valve procedure 12 years ago returns with heart failure and a hoarse voice. Learners link hoarseness to a very large left atrium and review follow-up care after valve treatment.

title: Lateral medullary syndrome resulting from atrial fibrillation due to rheumatic heart disease: A case report and literature review
brief: A 35-year-old breastfeeding woman in Nepal with known rheumatic heart disease comes in with sudden speech loss, right-sided weakness and chest pain. Learners connect atrial fibrillation in RHD with stroke and discuss anticoagulation.

title: Flaky Paint Dermatosis in Kwashiorkor
brief: A 3-month-old infant in Pondicherry, India, has scaly skin, 6 weeks of diarrhea, poor weight gain, dehydration and swelling. Learners recognize kwashiorkor signs and take a feeding history from the mother.

title: An infant with kwashiorkor: The forgotten disease
learner: Primary care trainees, nurses, community health workers
license: Free to read; copyright Academy of Family Physicians of Malaysia
brief: A 5-month-old boy in Malaysia develops kwashiorkor after improper weaning that went unnoticed. Learners take a weaning and feeding history in primary care and refer early.
learners: Primary care trainees, nurses, community health workers

title: Hepatocellular carcinoma with vertebral metastasis in a child with hepatitis B virus infection: a case report
brief: A 10-year-old Ethiopian boy with hepatitis B has 10 days of leg paralysis and incontinence from liver cancer that has spread to the spine. Learners discuss hepatitis B vaccination and breaking bad news to a family.

title: A case report of a teenager with hepatitis B surface antigen-positive multifocal hepatocellular carcinoma in a noncirrhotic liver
brief: A 13-year-old in Cape Coast, Ghana, with hepatitis B has advanced liver cancer, and her caregiver chooses palliative care. Learners practice a palliative care conversation with a caregiver.

title: Hepatitis B virus screening and vaccination in a family from Nigeria
license: Free to read; copyright Canadian Medical Association (CMAJ)
brief: A 42-year-old man born in Nigeria brings his 7-year-old daughter for a well-child visit, and the family has not been screened for hepatitis B. Learners counsel a migrant family on HBV screening and vaccination.

title: Verrucous carcinoma of buccal mucosa in female: a rare case scenario
brief: A 42-year-old woman in Tamil Nadu, India, who chews quid 7 to 8 times a day has had discomfort on the left side of her mouth for a week. Learners take a chewing habit history, examine the mouth and counsel on quitting.

title: HPV-Negative Oral Squamous Cell Carcinoma Arising from Oral Submucous Fibrosis with p16INK4A Positivity and Cellular Senescence: A Case Report
license: CC BY (Journal of Clinical and Experimental Dentistry)
brief: A 39-year-old man in Lucknow, India, with 10 years of gutkha chewing has advanced oral submucous fibrosis and cancer of the inner cheek. Learners link areca nut and gutkha use to oral cancer and screen for early lesions.

title: Challenges faced in managing cervical cancer patients who present post-operatively with more advanced disease in LMICs: Case studies from Cameroon
brief: Case 1 is a 37-year-old mother of three in Cameroon with pelvic pain, bleeding after sex and an abnormal VIA/VILI screen 2 years earlier that was not followed up. Learners explore barriers to cervical cancer care and counsel on next steps.

title: Tuberculosis of the Cervix Mimicking Cervical Carcinoma: A Case Report
brief: A 31-year-old woman in Nigeria with bleeding between periods and abnormal discharge, treated for cervical cancer, has cervical TB on biopsy. Learners take a gynecologic history and confirm a diagnosis with tissue before treatment.

title: Severe, acute watery diarrhea in an adult
brief: A 30-year-old woman from an informal settlement in Dhaka has 10 hours of sudden, large-volume watery diarrhea and vomiting. Learners assess dehydration, rehydrate and think of cholera.

title: The "first" case of cholera in Haiti: lessons for global health
brief: A 28-year-old man in central Haiti with untreated mental illness drinks river water and dies of acute watery diarrhea early in the 2010 outbreak. Learners discuss cholera recognition, mental health and community response.

title: Eclampsia
brief: A pregnant patient arrives confused and then has a seizure caused by eclampsia, and the team must also check on the fetus. Learners practice magnesium treatment, spotting magnesium toxicity, and calling obstetrics in time.

title: Eclampsia
brief: An oral board case in which the examiner plays a patient with new seizures from eclampsia. Learners take a full history and exam, give IV magnesium and blood pressure medicine, and discuss definitive care.

title: Clinical Decision-Making Case: Seizing the Diagnosis: Eclampsia
brief: A board exam style decision case about a patient whose seizure turns out to be eclampsia. Learners say aloud how they reach the diagnosis and pick the right treatment and disposition.

title: Posterior Reversible Encephalopathy Syndrome and Eclampsia
brief: A structured interview case about a woman with eclampsia and posterior reversible encephalopathy syndrome (PRES). Learners explain their thinking as they manage blood pressure, seizures and the underlying cause.

title: Out-of-Hospital Delivery of a Live Newborn Requiring Resuscitation
brief: A baby born outside the hospital arrives in the emergency department with breathing problems. Learners assess the newborn and follow the steps of neonatal resuscitation, with a focus on airway and breathing support.

title: Precipitous Birth
learner: residents, medical students, advanced practice providers
brief: A woman gives birth quickly in the emergency department, so the team must care for mother and baby at the same time. Learners recognize imminent delivery, manage bleeding after birth, and assess the newborn for resuscitation.
learners: residents, medical students, advanced practice providers

title: High Fidelity In Situ Shoulder Dystocia Simulation
brief: A woman in labor delivers in the emergency department and the baby's shoulders get stuck. Learners call the right help early and perform the maneuvers that free the baby.

title: Peripartum Cardiomyopathy
brief: A woman near the time of childbirth presents short of breath from new heart failure of pregnancy. Learners work up the pregnant patient, recognize peripartum cardiomyopathy, and treat heart failure.

title: Managing Spontaneous Abortion Hemorrhage: An Adult Simulation Case for Emergency Medicine Residents
brief: A woman has heavy bleeding after a miscarriage and becomes unstable. Learners recognize the hemorrhage, give uterotonic medicines and blood, and place a uterine balloon to stop bleeding.

title: Septic Abortion Complicated by Disseminated Intravascular Coagulation
brief: A pregnant patient with fever and vaginal bleeding has an infected miscarriage that leads to a clotting failure. Learners give early antibiotics, replace blood products and involve obstetrics for source control.

title: Post-Termination Hemorrhage
brief: A woman goes into shock from heavy bleeding after a pregnancy termination. Learners resuscitate for hemorrhagic shock, work through causes of the bleeding, and decide when to start massive transfusion.

title: Critical Care Transport: Blunt Polytrauma in Pregnancy
brief: A 24-year-old pregnant woman fell down a flight of stairs and has pelvic and leg fractures with blood loss. Learners run a trauma survey adapted to pregnancy, give blood, apply a pelvic binder and check the fetal heart rate.

title: Car Accident and Respiratory Distress: A Trauma-Based Pneumothorax Simulation Case for Medical Students
brief: A patient has trouble breathing after a car crash and develops a tension pneumothorax. Early medical students practice a structured trauma assessment, read x-ray and ultrasound, and escalate care in time.

title: Owning the Trauma Bay: Teaching Trauma Resuscitation to Emergency Medicine Residents and Nurses through In-situ Simulation
brief: Two trauma cases played by standardized patients: an older adult on blood thinners who fell down stairs, and a road bike crash. Teams practice trauma roles and clear communication in the real emergency department, including a head injury and an unstable pelvic fracture.

title: Acute Ischemic Stroke
brief: A patient arrives with sudden stroke symptoms. New residents practice the stroke scale, fast workup and the steps to decide on clot-busting treatment.

title: Clinical Decision Making: Acute Ischemic Stroke with Large Vessel Occlusion
brief: A board exam style decision case about a patient with a large-vessel stroke. Learners explain the key history, tests to rule out stroke mimics, acute treatment and where the patient should go.

title: Acute Exacerbation of COPD
brief: A patient with COPD has a severe flare and gets worse despite first treatment. Learners give the right medicines, start non-invasive ventilation, intubate, and find a pneumothorax after intubation.

title: Adolescent with Diabetic Ketoacidosis, Hypothermia and Pneumomediastinum
brief: A 12-year-old boy arrives drowsy, short of breath and cold, and has new-onset diabetic ketoacidosis. Learners diagnose and treat DKA and learn safe ventilator settings if the child needs intubation.

title: Diabetic Ketoacidosis and Necrotizing Soft Tissue Infection
brief: An oral board case of a patient in diabetic ketoacidosis caused by a severe flesh-eating skin infection. Learners treat DKA, start antibiotics, get surgery involved and explain the plan to the patient.

title: In-Flight Emergency: Altered Mental Status Secondary to Hypoglycemia
brief: A passenger with insulin-treated diabetes becomes confused during a flight because of low blood sugar. Learners use limited in-flight equipment to recognize and treat hypoglycemia.

title: Posterior Reversible Encephalopathy Syndrome (PRES)
brief: A patient has a hypertensive emergency with brain symptoms caused by posterior reversible encephalopathy syndrome (PRES). Learners recognize the syndrome and lower blood pressure safely with IV drugs.

title: Telemedicine Consult for Shortness of Breath Due to Sympathetic Crashing Acute Pulmonary Edema
brief: A patient suddenly becomes very short of breath with very high blood pressure and fluid in the lungs, and the doctor guides care by video. Learners treat acute heart failure with nitrates and ventilation support and avoid chasing the fast heart rhythm.

title: Acute Pulmonary Edema and NSTEMI
brief: An oral board case of a critically ill patient with fluid in the lungs and a heart attack (NSTEMI). Learners work up the breathlessness and treat with preload and afterload reduction, diuretics and ventilation support.

title: Reassessment Case: Acute Pulmonary Edema in a Boarding Patient
brief: A standardized patient who is waiting for a hospital bed suddenly gets worse with fluid in the lungs. Learners reassess, change the plan and treat pulmonary edema.

title: Alcohol Withdrawal with Delirium Tremens
learner: residents, medical students, advanced practice providers
brief: A patient with heavy alcohol use arrives confused and shaking from severe withdrawal. Learners use the CIWA score, give benzodiazepines and manage delirium tremens.
learners: residents, medical students, advanced practice providers

title: Alcohol Withdrawal
brief: An oral board case of a patient with alcohol withdrawal that can progress to seizures and delirium. Learners assess severity and treat withdrawal safely.

title: Altered Mental Status: Epilepsy, Acute Psychosis, Intoxication or Delirium Tremens?
brief: A confused, agitated patient could have a seizure disorder, psychosis or intoxication, but the cause is delirium tremens. Learners sort the differential and treat promptly with benzodiazepines.

title: Opioid Overdose Simulation in Medical Student Education
brief: An unresponsive patient has slow breathing and pinpoint pupils from an opioid overdose. Students recognize the signs, support breathing with a bag-valve mask and give naloxone quickly.

title: Tricyclic Antidepressant Overdose
brief: An oral board case of a confused patient who took an intentional overdose of a tricyclic antidepressant. Learners read the typical ECG changes and treat with sodium bicarbonate.

title: Beta-Blocker Toxicity
brief: A patient with low blood pressure and a slow heart rate has taken too much of a beta-blocker. Learners work through shock, use high-dose insulin and other treatments, and discuss suicide risk.

title: Agitated Psychiatric Patient
brief: A standardized patient plays a very agitated person with a psychiatric illness. Learners look for medical causes, try verbal calming, choose safe sedation, and keep themselves and staff safe.

title: Managing Conflict Case: Admission of a Patient with Decompensated Schizophrenia, Hypertension, and Diabetes
brief: A short exam station where the examiner plays consultants who disagree about admitting a patient with worsening schizophrenia plus high blood pressure and diabetes. Learners practice resolving conflict for the patient's benefit.

title: Meningococcal Meningitis with Waterhouse-Friderichsen Syndrome
brief: A confused patient with fever and rash has meningococcal meningitis and gets worse into septic shock with bleeding. Learners resuscitate, give early antibiotics, manage the bleeding and decide on prophylaxis for contacts.

title: Sepsis Secondary to an Abdominal Wound Infection
brief: A patient with an infected abdominal wound progresses to septic shock. Learners give fluids, antibiotics and vasopressors following sepsis guidelines; the case can be run with a standardized patient.

title: Severe Sepsis Manifesting as A-Fib with Rapid Ventricular Rate
brief: An adult with an infected pressure ulcer presents with a fast irregular heart rhythm caused by sepsis. Learners find the source with a careful exam and treat the sepsis first.

title: Pediatric Sepsis Case Scenario
brief: A child presents with sepsis that is easy to miss. Emergency nurses practice early recognition and fast treatment of pediatric sepsis.

title: Pediatric Toxic Shock Syndrome
learner: residents, medical students, advanced practice providers
brief: A child is critically ill with toxic shock syndrome. Learners search for the infection source and give aggressive fluids and antibiotics.
learners: residents, medical students, advanced practice providers

title: Clinical Decision-Making Case: Febrile Infant
brief: A board style case of a newborn under 28 days old with fever who may look well. Learners order a full sepsis workup including lumbar puncture and start antibiotics.

title: Procedural Case: Neonatal Lumbar Puncture
brief: A procedure station with a task trainer in which learners do a lumbar puncture on a febrile newborn. It trains the skill needed to check for meningitis in young infants.

title: Acute Chest Syndrome
brief: An oral board case of a patient with sickle cell disease who has chest pain, low oxygen and repeated requests for pain relief. Learners diagnose acute chest syndrome, give pain medicine, antibiotics and oxygen, and admit to intensive care.

title: Massive Upper Gastrointestinal Bleeding
brief: A patient faints and vomits blood from bleeding esophageal varices due to cirrhosis, and refuses blood products for religious reasons. Learners manage the bloody airway, use alternatives to transfusion and place a balloon tamponade tube.

title: Status Asthmaticus
brief: A patient arrives in a severe, life-threatening asthma attack. Learners give the right medicines, decide when to intubate and set the ventilator safely.

title: Primary Measles Encephalitis
brief: A child with fever, rash and confusion has brain inflammation from measles. Learners ask about vaccination and travel, use airborne isolation, start empiric treatment and arrange transfer.

title: Febrile Seizure Simulation
brief: A young child has a seizure with fever. Learners evaluate the child, look for the cause of the fever and educate the parents.

title: Managing STEMIs without a Catheterization Lab: A Simulated Scenario to Improve Emergency Clinician Recognition and Execution of Thrombolysis in the Setting of Rural STEMI Management
learner: residents, medical students, advanced practice providers
brief: A patient with a heart attack arrives at a rural emergency department with no heart catheter lab. Learners diagnose STEMI, discuss risks and benefits of clot-busting drugs with the patient, give thrombolysis and arrange transfer.
learners: residents, medical students, advanced practice providers

title: Chest Pain with Acute Coronary Syndrome
brief: A patient with chest pain turns out to have a heart attack on the ECG. Learners build a differential, give the right medicines and arrange care; the case can be run with a standardized patient.

title: Prioritization: Run This Board: Septic Shock, Acute Coronary Syndrome, Small Bowel Obstruction, and Penetrating Chest Trauma
brief: A multi-patient station where the learner must care for several sick patients at once, including septic shock and a heart attack. Learners practice deciding who needs care first and stabilizing them.

title: Pediatric Simulation-Based Prehospital Training Course in Botswana
brief: A two day course built for ambulance crews in Botswana with five low-cost child scenarios, including diarrhea with shock, newborn delivery, seizure, asthma and a vehicle rollover. Providers practice pediatric resuscitation with rapid cycle deliberate practice.

title: A Simulation and Small-Group Pediatric Emergency Medicine Course for Generalist Healthcare Providers: Gastrointestinal and Nutrition Emergencies
brief: A course used in Belize with simulation cases of children with gastroenteritis and dehydration, bowel obstruction, and malnutrition complicated by sepsis or low blood sugar. General providers practice recognizing and stabilizing these children in low-resource settings.

title: A Pediatric Emergency Medicine Refresher Course for Generalist Healthcare Providers in Belize: Respiratory Emergencies
brief: A refresher course used in Belize with simulation cases of children with pneumonia and asthma, plus teaching on bronchiolitis and airway care. General providers practice spotting breathing emergencies and managing the child's airway.

title: A Simulation-Based Course for Prehospital Providers in a Developing Emergency Medical Response System
brief: A course built for ambulance crews in Botswana with scenarios such as a cyclist hit by a vehicle, heart failure breathlessness, heavy vaginal bleeding with shock and a weak patient with low blood sugar. Providers practice assessment and stabilization in the field.

title: Clinical Decision-Making Case: Non-Accidental Trauma
brief: A board style case of a child with injuries that turn out to be from abuse. Learners take the right history, spot suspicious exam findings, order tests for hidden injuries and plan a safe disposition.

title: Identification of a Human Trafficking Victim: A Simulation
brief: A patient in the emergency department shows warning signs of human trafficking. Learners assess the patient, separate them safely from the possible trafficker and connect them to help.

title: Abdominal Pain and Vaginal Discharge: An Eye-Opening Simulation Case about Human Trafficking
brief: A patient comes in with abdominal pain and vaginal discharge and is a hidden victim of human trafficking. Learners recognize the signs and respond; the case also fits clinics and prehospital settings.

title: Patient-Centered Communication Case: Threatened Miscarriage
brief: A standardized patient with early pregnancy bleeding is anxious about losing the pregnancy. Learners practice empathy, explore the patient's concerns and explain management options clearly.

title: Severe Hyperkalemia
brief: A case report of a 78-year-old man with end-stage kidney disease and chest pain whose ECG shows dangerously high potassium. It teaches treating hyperkalemia from the ECG before lab results return.

title: A Case of Community-Acquired Tuberculosis in an Infant Presenting with Pneumonia Refractory to Antibiotic Therapy
brief: A case report of a 7-week-old infant with pneumonia that does not improve with antibiotics and poor growth, later found to have disseminated TB. It teaches when to think of TB in infants and to image the brain.

title: A Case Report on Miliary Tuberculosis in Acute Immune Reconstitution Inflammatory Syndrome
brief: A case report of a man with HIV who gets worse cough and fever two weeks after starting antiretroviral therapy, from miliary TB with immune reconstitution syndrome. It shows the classic chest x-ray and treatment with steroids.

title: CHF Exacerbation
brief: A patient with untreated high blood pressure who takes a lot of ibuprofen has a week of worsening breathlessness from heart failure. Learners treat low oxygen, control blood pressure with nitrates and manage the airway if breathing fails.

title: STEMI with Ventricular Tachycardia
brief: A patient with chest pain has a heart attack on the ECG and then develops a dangerous fast heart rhythm and cardiac arrest. Learners give aspirin, activate the cath lab and follow ACLS for VT and VF.

title: Status Asthmaticus with AutoPEEP (Pediatric)
brief: A child in a severe asthma attack speaks only two words at a time and needs intubation, then worsens on the ventilator. Learners step up asthma treatment, intubate and recognize air trapping (auto-PEEP).

learners: Nursing students (prelicensure); adaptable for other health learners

brief: Butch, 68, is a homeless veteran with uncontrolled type 2 diabetes and an infected toe who needs surgery. Learners assess the wound, teach about diet and medicines, and plan discharge around housing and other social needs.
learners: Nursing students (prelicensure); adaptable for other health learners

title: Eugene Shaw (ACE.V veterans unfolding case)

license: Free to download for teaching; copyright National League for Nursing (no open license stated)
brief: Eugene, 87, a Korean War veteran with hypertension, type 2 diabetes, tobacco and alcohol use, has leg pain from a blocked artery and needs bypass surgery. Learners give pre- and post-operative care, check medicine adherence and plan lifestyle change at discharge.
learners: Nursing students (prelicensure); adaptable for other health learners

title: Jenny Brown (ACE.V veterans unfolding case)

license: Free to download for teaching; copyright National League for Nursing (no open license stated)
brief: Jenny, 29, is a pregnant Iraq veteran admitted with severe anxiety after learning her baby will have a cleft lip and palate; the case follows her through antenatal and postpartum care. Learners screen for anxiety, depression, suicide risk, PTSD and brain injury.
learners: Nursing students (prelicensure); adaptable for other health learners

license: Free to download for teaching; copyright National League for Nursing (no open license stated)
brief: Randy, 32, an Iraq veteran with PTSD and headaches, comes to the emergency department confused after a car crash. Learners assess mental and neurological status, review PTSD treatment and support him and his family over several weeks.
learners: Nursing students (prelicensure); adaptable for other health learners

brief: Patrick, 64, has an above-knee amputation from a war injury, arthritis and heart failure; he is seen in clinic, admitted for heart failure, then followed at home. Learners practice respectful communication with a person with a disability, focused assessment and patient teaching.
learners: Nursing students (prelicensure); adaptable for other health learners

title: Mary Lou and Rob Brady (ACE.D disabilities unfolding case)

learners: Nursing students (prelicensure); adaptable for other health learners

title: mhGAP Depression module role plays (assessment and management)
learner: Non-specialist primary care workers (doctors, nurses, clinical officers)
brief: A person comes to a health center feeling sad and exhausted for two months, sleeping badly and afraid of losing their job; one version is a 27-year-old who lost his bank job after a broken engagement. Learners use the mhGAP guide to assess for depression, rule out other causes such as past mania or thyroid disease, and plan care.
learners: Non-specialist primary care workers (doctors, nurses, clinical officers)

title: mhGAP Self-harm/suicide module role plays
brief: Scripts include a 30-year-old woman with postnatal depression recovering on the ward after drinking pesticide, and an 18-year-old woman who cut her arms after a fight with her father. Learners practice asking directly about suicide, assessing risk and planning psychosocial follow-up.

title: mhGAP Alcohol and drug use module role plays
brief: One patient returns after a hypertension diagnosis and drinks 10 to 12 drinks a day with shaking when he stops; another, Mr Sana, is a weekend binge drinker worried about blackouts. Learners assess alcohol use with the mhGAP algorithm and use brief motivational interviewing.

title: mhGAP Dementia module role plays (assessment and follow-up)
brief: Farah brings her mother Ingrid, 73, who is forgetful, struggles with cooking and word finding, and later wanders at night and falls. Learners assess the person and the carer for dementia, then manage behavior, safety and carer stress at follow-up.

brief: Stan, 51, a busy store owner, was told he had diabetes six months ago, ran out of metformin and now has a random glucose of 12 mmol/L. In 11 minutes the candidate takes a focused history and counsels him on management options.
learners: International medical graduates and final-year medical students

title: NAC Examination sample case study: Sandrine Thomas
learner: International medical graduates and final-year medical students
license: Free for exam preparation; copyright Medical Council of Canada
brief: Sandrine, 45, a chef, needs foot surgery and is afraid that opioid pain medicine will make her relapse after past drug use 10 years ago. The candidate takes a focused history, makes a safe discharge pain plan and counsels her.
learners: International medical graduates and final-year medical students

title: Assessing suicide risk and responding
license: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 (free Simulation Canada account needed to download)
brief: A virtual patient needs a mental health and suicide risk assessment. Learners use the SAFE-T protocol with the Columbia scale, identify warning signs and protective factors, and make a safe care plan.

title: Acute stroke assessment
license: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 (free Simulation Canada account needed to download)
brief: A patient with an acute stroke, played by a patient actor or a high-fidelity manikin. Learners assess the patient with the Canadian Neurological Scale, based on Canadian stroke best practice guidance.

title: Neonatal resuscitation and surfactant administration
authors: Herman H, Armstrong K, Bassant M
license: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 (free Simulation Canada account needed to download)
brief: A 34-year-old mother with preeclampsia and threatened preterm labor has an emergency cesarean birth, and the preterm baby needs help to breathe. Learners work with the team to resuscitate and stabilize the newborn and give surfactant.

title: Delirium
license: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 (free Simulation Canada account needed to download)
brief: A 79-year-old with hypertension and mild dementia is two days after hip fracture surgery. Learners recognize delirium on top of dementia in an extended reality simulation.

learners: Nursing students in maternal-child or mental health practice

learners: Nursing and other health learners and practitioners
